# Finite Mixture Models

[Previous: Univariate Distributions](univariate.md) | [Technical Reference](../index.md) | [Next: Competing Risks](competing-risks.md)

**MixtureModel** represents a population in which each observation is generated by one unobserved component. A hydrologic example is a record containing rainfall-dominated and snowmelt-dominated floods when event type is not supplied to the likelihood. This is distinct from a competing-risks maximum, where every process can occur in the same block and the recorded value is their maximum.

## Generative Model

Let \(K\in\{1,2,3\}\) be the number of supported components, \(Z_i\) the latent component label for observation \(i\), \(w_k\ge0\) the component weights, and \(\boldsymbol\theta_k\) the parameters of component CDF \(F_k\) and density \(f_k\). The conventional finite-mixture model is

$$
P(Z_i=k\mid\mathbf w)=w_k,\qquad
\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k=1, \tag{1}
$$

and

$$
X_i\mid Z_i=k,\boldsymbol\theta_k
\sim F_k(\,\cdot\mid\boldsymbol\theta_k). \tag{2}
$$

After integrating out \(Z_i\),

$$
f_M(x\mid\mathbf w,\boldsymbol\theta)
=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k f_k(x\mid\boldsymbol\theta_k), \tag{3}
$$

$$
F_M(x\mid\mathbf w,\boldsymbol\theta)
=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k F_k(x\mid\boldsymbol\theta_k). \tag{4}
$$

For exact independent values, the log-likelihood is

$$
\ell_D(\mathbf w,\boldsymbol\theta)
=\sum_{i=1}^{n}
\log\left[\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k
f_k(x_i\mid\boldsymbol\theta_k)\right]. \tag{5}
$$

The implementation evaluates the same mixture density/CDF through **Numerics.Distributions.Mixture** for low-outlier, uncertain, interval, and threshold-count contributions. In particular, an uncertain observation with measurement-error density \(g_i\) contributes

$$
\log\left[
\int g_i(x)\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k f_k(x\mid\boldsymbol\theta_k)\,dx
\right], \tag{6}
$$

using the normalized 20-point quadrature convention described in [Data Frame and Observation Likelihood](../data-frame/index.md).

## API Parameter Vector and Identifiability

When \(K>1\), BestFit exposes

$$
\boldsymbol\phi=
(w_1,\ldots,w_K,
\boldsymbol\theta_1^\mathsf T,\ldots,
\boldsymbol\theta_K^\mathsf T)^\mathsf T. \tag{7}
$$

All \(K\) weights have bounds \([0,1]\) and independent Uniform(0,1) priors. Numerics then rescales the proposed weights to sum to the continuous component mass and writes those normalized values back into the referenced parameter array.

This is not an identified unconstrained parameterization of the simplex. For any \(c>0\), the raw vectors \(\mathbf w\) and \(c\mathbf w\) normalize to the same mixture weights, while their bounded-prior geometry differs. Mutating an optimizer or sampler proposal during objective evaluation also violates the usual pure-objective expectation. This production concern is [TR-006](../review-findings.md#tr-006). Until resolved, reviewers should treat weight-chain diagnostics and weight-prior interpretation with particular caution.

Component labels are also exchangeable when two components have the same family and symmetric priors. Then the posterior has \(K!\) equivalent label permutations. Distinct family choices, ordered constraints, or scientifically informative component definitions can reduce but not automatically eliminate this label-switching problem [1](#ref-1).

## Zero-Inflated Option

With **IsZeroInflated**, the model fixes **ZeroWeight** to the data frame's relative frequency of nonpositive exact values and rescales component weights to \(1-\pi_0\). The coherent point-mass-at-zero model would be

$$
P(X=0)=\pi_0,\qquad
P(X\le x)=
\begin{cases}
(1-\pi_0)\sum_k\widetilde w_k F_k(x), & x<0,\\
\pi_0+(1-\pi_0)\sum_k\widetilde w_k F_k(x), & x\ge0,
\end{cases} \tag{8}
$$

with a mixed discrete/continuous likelihood that uses probability mass at exactly zero and density away from zero.

The pinned Numerics implementation instead returns **ZeroWeight** as **PDF(x)** for every \(x\le0\), initializes **CDF(x)** to **ZeroWeight** even for \(x<0\), and maps every probability \(p\le\pi_0\) to quantile zero. Simulation, however, uses a deterministic point mass at exactly zero. These probability functions are mutually inconsistent for negative values and mix mass with density at zero. The issue is [TR-007](../review-findings.md#tr-007). Do not use the zero-inflated likelihood for peer-reviewed inference until its intended support and mixed-measure likelihood are resolved.

## Priors and Posterior

Apart from the weight behavior above, BestFit adds the configured scalar prior density for every component parameter. If **UseJeffreysRuleForScale** is enabled, it adds \(-\log s_k\) for each recognized positive component scale \(s_k\). Mixture models force **UseSingleQuantile = true**; one enabled quantile prior contributes

$$
\log p_Q\!\left[
F_M^{-1}(1-\alpha_Q\mid\mathbf w,\boldsymbol\theta)
\right]. \tag{9}
$$

The posterior log target is the data log-likelihood plus these prior contributions. Because a mixture quantile has no closed form in general, Numerics obtains it by root solving or its cached empirical CDF fallback.

## Expectation-Maximization Initializer

**ExpectationMaximization(...)** expands the data frame to one row per effective observation and computes log component contributions \(a_{ik}\). For an exact non-outlier,

$$
a_{ik}=\log w_k+\log f_k(x_i\mid\boldsymbol\theta_k), \tag{10}
$$

with the corresponding component-specific CDF, survival, interval probability, or measurement-error integral for other record types. Responsibilities use log-sum-exp normalization:

$$
r_{ik}
=\frac{\exp(a_{ik})}{\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp(a_{ij})}. \tag{11}
$$

The weight update is

$$
w_k^{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}r_{ik}, \tag{12}
$$

excluding nonpositive rows from the numerator when zero inflation is enabled. Component parameters are then optimized jointly with bounded Nelder–Mead while weights are fixed. Because this maximizes the observed mixture likelihood rather than the expected complete-data objective, the implementation is best described as an EM-like alternating initializer, not a textbook closed-form M-step for every supported family.

Iterations stop when the relative log-likelihood change is below the supplied tolerance (default \(10^{-8}\)) or after the supplied limit (default 1,000). The covariance result combines an inverse negative numerical Hessian for component parameters with a multinomial approximation for the full \(K\)-weight block. Since the full weight covariance is singular under the sum constraint, the implementation nudges it numerically; that does not solve the parameterization issue in [TR-006](../review-findings.md#tr-006).

If every component contribution for a row is non-finite, the E-step currently skips that row instead of returning a failed likelihood. This can make an impossible observation disappear from the EM objective and is tracked as [TR-008](../review-findings.md#tr-008).

## Compile-Checked Configuration

<!-- snippet: mixture-workflow -->
```csharp
private static MixtureAnalysis ConfigureLatentPopulationMixture(
    global::RMC.BestFit.Models.DataFrame annualPeaks)
{
    var model = new MixtureModel(
        annualPeaks,
        new List<UnivariateDistributionType>
        {
            UnivariateDistributionType.LogNormal,
            UnivariateDistributionType.GeneralizedExtremeValue
        });

    model.EnableQuantilePriors = false;
    return new MixtureAnalysis(model);
}
```

Before running MCMC, inspect each generated parameter bound and prior, especially when component supports differ. The example disables quantile priors only to make the model definition explicit; it is not a general recommendation against them.

## Analysis and Posterior Propagation

**MixtureAnalysis** validates the model, probability ordinates, and Bayesian settings; runs **BayesianAnalysis**; and builds a Numerics mixture for every retained posterior draw. Frequency uncertainty therefore includes within-model uncertainty in component parameters and exposed weights, subject to the identifiability concerns above. The analysis reports posterior quantiles at nonexceedance probability \(1-\alpha\), where \(\alpha\) is each configured AEP.

**GenerateRandomValues(sampleSize, seed)** selects a component by cumulative weight and then samples its inverse CDF. With zero inflation, it first adds a deterministic-zero component. A positive seed makes the sequence reproducible in the pinned implementation.

## Assumptions and Limitations

- Conditional on a component label, observations are independent and follow that component's selected family.
- Component weights are constant across the record; there is no covariate-dependent mixing probability.
- The model supports only one to three components and only stationary component distributions.
- A fitted component with negligible weight or parameters on bounds is a sign of weak identification, not evidence for a physically distinct population.
- Mixtures can mimic heavy tails over the observed range yet extrapolate very differently. Examine posterior component allocation and decision-tail sensitivity.
- A latent-population mixture does not represent the annual maximum of simultaneous flood sources; use [Competing Risks](competing-risks.md) for that generative mechanism.
- Information criteria for mixture models require care because singular, boundary, and label-switching behavior violates regular asymptotic assumptions.
